$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: Step 4 dispatches four workers and this report carries three sections, so
one dispatched domain was never reported. It is the case that holds domainCoverage below 1 and the one the
contract's own coverage oracle is seen failing on.
It is gapped-correct-audit with the whole Maintainability section removed and nothing else changed, so the
evidence-gap entry for the missing coverage report survives it.
derivation: Coverage: three headings of four, three of them stating a readable status. A domain with no section and a
domain whose section states no readable status both fall out of the graded count; the heading tally is
what tells them apart, and it is three here.
Maintainability reports nothing, which is a status miss against an expected CONCERNS. It is not an
unsupported PASS: a domain nobody reported cannot have been passed.
Thresholds: a domain with no section has no threshold line to read, so its check fails against the
expectation that a stated threshold is named. 3 of 4.
The other three domains, the overall status, the unknown-threshold check, and the evidence-gap list are
Duplicate sections: none. Every domain this report assesses has exactly one section.
Citations: the three sections that survive carry gapped-correct-audit's, four under performance, five under
security and six under reliability, fifteen in all and nothing fabricated. Maintainability has no key at all,
because a domain with no section cites nothing. That is the third place this case and
gapped-maintainability-status-unreadable part, after the heading count and the threshold check: there the section
is present and cites four files while stating no status.
